questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was different from my one culture, but also within close distance to home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, a lot of information meetings and emails

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got assistance in showing us the school, and them explaining how its was to be enrolled in the different classes etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy if you are willing to spend the same amount of money on rent in Porto as you are at home. I lived in a big student accomodation building with fitness and a study hall, i can recomend  finding one of these which there are a lot of around campus also.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to find an apartment in the city centre you should be out in good time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was an online application and then an online meeting once you arrived at porto, whereafter you needed to go to the main office to pick up your student card.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email correspondence with the erasmus in office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful. Although it is a confusing system. You don't know at what time the different classes and exams are, so the first courses you select blindly, and them have to figure out if you can switch courses once everyone is enrolled. This is quite tedious, and you can only select the courses that are not full. takes a long time to get them approved and a lot of uncertainty around it. I was lucky but i had a few friends who weren't. Just an inefficient sysem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the levels of the courses were true to what I was expecting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, one teacher giving a lesson, sometimes where we did exercises. Only difference is that it is smaller classes than at UCPH. And also that you can get distributed evaluation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Data Analysis, Macroeconomic Policy, International Trade, Corporate Finance, Financial Markets

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think the course MAcroeconomic Policy was very interesting. The teacher was good at making it relevant with presentations of new papers where the different policies were at use, so you could see it in practice.

questions.answer: I had to buy a lot of stuff for my apartment, i thought there were blankets, pillows and kitchen stuff, but i had to buy everything.

questions.answer: I didn't really research or participate in anything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really research or participate in anything

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit all other parts of Portugal. It is an amazing country to travel around in. Also the smaller one-day trips to places around Porto. Very easy with the train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was tough in the beginning, but you find your way quicker than you first fear upon arrival.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the students networks, either Erasmus Porto or Erasmus Student Network Porto (ESN)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are often late. And a lot of people talk in class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go explore, drink a lot of Portwine and enjoy it while it lasts.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: i can't think of anything

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home, and feeling alone in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
